newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbek Central Bank mends currency regulations.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek Central Bank mends currency regulations.

text.p: Uzbekistan's Central Bank said on Wednesday it was introducing a new system for setting the official rate of the national sum currency and said the new scheme would better reflect market-economy principles.

A central bank statement said exchange rates for accountancy, taxation, customs and other purposes would be set once a week and take into account street rates and volumes on the local exchange and over-the-counter markets.
Until now, the rate was pegged to twice-weekly trading sessions on the currency exchange.
The statement also said the bank would take into consideration the rates and volumes of cash transactions, changes in money supply and inflation when setting rates.
It said the changes were aimed at creating an over-the-counter currency market, but provided no details.
Official exchange rates of around 55 sum to the dollar are far below black market rates of 100 and higher.

A local commercial bank official who declined to be named told Reuters the new mechanism could be an attempt by the central bank to please the International Monetary Fund, whose mission is scheduled to visit Tashkent at the end of this month.
The IMF said in November it was withholding a $185 million stand-by loan to Uzbekistan because of high inflation and restrictions imposed by Tashkent on currency operations.
